correctness.rationale: For every existing vertex, the exact conditional leafneighbour-minus-half-degree increment is I/2-J, producing the linear drift factor 1-1/[2(n-1)], increments bounded by 2, and conditional variance at most degree/(n-1). The exact expected squared-degree sum 2(n-1)H_(n-1) makes the maximum degree at most sqrt(n) log n with probability tending to 1. A stopped deterministic-weight Freedman argument and union bound yield a uniform O_P(n^(1/4)(log n)^2) approximation. Exact rising-factorial moments establish a positive half-normal root-degree lower anchor on the sqrt(n) scale. The deterministic maxima comparison then proves L_n/D_n ->1/2 in probability. A standalone exact-rational finite-state checker passed 53,992 assertions and seeded diagnostics, but no finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A 2026 primary publication explicitly conjectures this ratio, making the gap substantive rather than arbitrary. Fixed-degree concentration is not a solution because a maximum over n dependent vertices occurs at order sqrt(n) degree. The new uniform martingale theorem provides a quantitative whole-tree comparison and resolves the exact natural invariant 1/2, not a small or routine parameter substitution. The limitation to the canonical model and unoptimized logarithmic factors are explicitly stated.
